name: ST25R3911B-AQFT
title: ST25R3911B: 13.56 MHz HF reader / NFC initiator IC, 1.4 W differential antenna drivers, VHBR, automatic antenna tuning, QFN32 / VFQFPN32
summary: A 13.56 MHz reader front end with protocol framing for ISO 14443A and B (with high and very high bit rates), ISO 15693, FeliCa and NFCIP-1 (ISO 18092) initiator and active target. Two push-pull antenna drivers of about 1 Ω each drive an antenna LC tank differentially (up to 1.4 W) or single ended, and AM and PM receive channels with automatic gain control demodulate the tag reply. A host talks to it over a 4-wire SPI up to 6 Mbit/s with a 96-byte FIFO; stream and transparent modes let the host do the framing for other protocols. For low-power card detection it carries a capacitive sensor, phase and amplitude measurement of the antenna tank and a wake-up timer on a 32 kHz RC oscillator; trim pins switch external capacitors for antenna tuning. VDD runs from 2.4 V to 5.5 V and the host interface from 1.65 V to 5.5 V.

operation.text: Access control, e-government, ticketing, payment (EMVCo 2.6b) and NFC infrastructure.

Inside: crystal oscillator, three regulators with power-on reset and bias, transmitter (RFO1, RFO2), receiver (RFI1, RFI2), an A/D converter fed by a phase and amplitude detector, external field detector, capacitive sensor (CSI, CSO), RC oscillator with wake-up timer, framing, FIFO, control logic and an SPI with level shifters to the host.

The drivers on RFO1 and RFO2 work single sided or differentially and include a modulator for OOK or adjustable AM. They are meant to drive an antenna on the same board directly, without a 50 Ω cable; a 50 Ω cable also works, with some advanced features lost.

Two receive chains, one for AM and one for PM, each a peak detector or mixer followed by two gain and filter stages and a slicer. Filters adapt to mode and bit rate; subcarriers from 212 kHz to 6.8 MHz are supported.

The phase detector compares the phase of the driver outputs (RFO1, RFO2) with the receiver inputs (RFI1, RFI2); the amplitude detector self-mixes the RFI signals, whose amplitude follows the antenna tank voltage. Both serve PM demodulation and checking and optimising antenna tuning.

Measures the capacitance between two copper electrodes on CSI and CSO. A reference taken at calibration stands for the surroundings; a periodic measurement that departs from it by more than a register threshold raises an interrupt.

A low-power detector used in NFC mode with two thresholds: peer detection (an initiator field in NFCIP-1 target mode, or the target field in active initiator mode) and collision avoidance (any RF field during the NFCIP-1 collision avoidance procedure).

Runs with a 13.56 MHz or 27.12 MHz crystal. Its transconductance is raised at start-up for a fast start, and an interrupt reports a stable oscillation since start-up time depends on crystal and temperature. VHBR operation needs the 27.12 MHz crystal. The oscillator also feeds MCU_CLK as set in IO configuration register 1.

Three regulators, each with its own blocking capacitor (analog VSP_A, digital VSP_D, antenna drivers VSP_RF), give the reader high PSRR; in 3.3 V supply mode they share one regulated voltage. The Adjust regulators command measures VDD at maximum load and sets the regulated voltage 250 mV below it, shown in the Regulator and timer display register; the voltage can also be written directly in the Regulator voltage control register. The block also makes the analog reference AGD, which takes its own capacitor.

In receive the framing block finds SOF, EOF and data bits from the demodulated subcarrier, checks parity and CRC and writes bytes into the FIFO; in transmit it takes FIFO bytes, adds parity, CRC, SOF and EOF and encodes the modulation. In transparent mode framing and FIFO are bypassed: the sliced subcarrier goes straight to MISO and MOSI drives the modulator directly.

The part runs from 2.4 V to 5.5 V on VDD and 1.65 V to 5.5 V on VDD_IO, the host on SPI with IRQ and MCU_CLK, a crystal with load capacitors on XTI and XTO, blocking capacitors on AGD and the three regulator outputs, and the antenna through an EMC filter (series inductor, shunt capacitor) and a series capacitor into a parallel tank, with capacitive dividers feeding RFI1 and RFI2. Single-sided driving uses RFO1 only and leaves the TRIM pins open; differential driving uses both outputs.

The Operation control register sets the mode. At power-up it is all zero and the part is in power-down: only POR and part of the bias run, the regulators are transparent, and the SPI still works so every register can be set. Setting en starts the crystal oscillator and regulators (ready mode) and an interrupt follows when the oscillator is stable. rx_en and tx_en switch receiver and transmitter separately, for example to keep the field on with the receiver off, or to receive only in NFCIP-1 active mode. Setting wu with all other bits 0 enters wake-up mode: the RC oscillator and wake-up timer schedule measurements and an interrupt wakes the host when one departs from its reference.

Two identical push-pull drivers on RFO1 and RFO2 drive the antenna tank differentially; IO configuration register 1 bit single uses only one. Each driver has eight binary-weighted segments; the MSB segment is 2 Ω typical and all segments together about 1 Ω. The non-modulated level normally has all segments on; switching some off in the RFO normal level definition register lowers antenna amplitude or Q without changing hardware. Single mode halves the number of tank components and reduces the output power, and lets two tanks on RFO1 and RFO2 be multiplexed with bit rfo2.

OOK and AM are selected with tr_am in the Auxiliary definition register. In OOK (ISO14443A) the drivers stop and the tank rings down with its Q; ook_hr puts the drivers in tristate during the pause to shorten the decay. AM (ISO14443B) raises the driver impedance by turning segments off; the modulated level can be calibrated to a target depth with the Calibrate modulation depth command.

For readers that need a slow field rise (STIF asks for 10 % to 90 % in 10 µs or longer), VSP_RF is collapsed while the transmitter is off and ramped when it is turned on: typically 15 µs at 3 V and 20 µs at 5 V. Procedure: with the transmitter off set slow_up (IO configuration register 2) and hold it at least 2 ms to discharge VSP_RF; turn on the transmitter; clear slow_up before sending any command.

The receiver demodulates the tag subcarrier (AM, PM or both), amplifies, band-pass filters and slices it, and runs RSSI, AGC and squelch. RFI1 and RFI2 normally come from capacitive dividers on the antenna coil terminals, so they are in phase with the coil voltage; the divider must keep their peaks below VSP_A. With both channels on, framing picks the channel automatically; rx_chn chooses one or both channels and rx_man manual or automatic selection. The internal signal rx_on, raised when the mask receive timer expires or by the Unmask receive data command, gates RSSI, AGC and framing.

AM demodulation by a peak detector or a mixer, chosen with amd_sel. The peak detector follows positive and negative peaks of one input (usually RFI1), gain 0.7, up to fc/8 (1700 kHz). The AM mixer rectifies both inputs synchronously, gain 0.55, and is made for VHBR (fc/8 and up); fc/4 and fc/2 need the mixer. The PM mixer gives 60 mV differential per 1 % phase change (16.67 mV/°), up to fc/8. With lf_en, LF signals on RFI1 and RFI2 bypass the demodulator for external demodulation.

Three stages: first and third first-order high pass, second a second-order low pass. First stage gain about 20 dB, reducible in six 2.5 dB steps, plus a 5.5 dB boost; it is lower for VHBR (fc/8, fc/4) and is set only through Receiver configuration register 3, whose default is minimum gain. Its zero is 60 kHz by default, or 40 kHz or 12 kHz. Second and third stage gain is 23 dB, reducible in six 3 dB steps, under AGC and squelch or set in Receiver configuration register 4; the Reset Rx gain command clears squelch and loads register 4 into the AGC shadow registers. The low-pass corner follows lp2 to lp0. Analog preset loads the recommended filter for each mode and bit rate.
A window comparator slices the subcarrier; its window has five settings in 3 dB steps from ±33 mV to ±120 mV, adjusted by AGC and squelch or set in Receiver configuration register 4.

AGC and squelch share eleven steps: from the default (smallest window, highest gain) the first four widen the slicer window by 3 dB each, the next six cut second and third stage gain by 3 dB each. The starting step comes from Receiver configuration register 4 and the Gain reduction state register shows the result. AGC is to be off during bit anticollision such as Type A.

Against noise from tag processing or surroundings: while the slicer output toggles more than twice in 50 µs, gain drops 3 dB and the next 50 µs is watched, until two or fewer transitions or maximum reduction. Reset Rx gain clears it. Automatic squelch (sqm_dyn) starts 18.88 µs after the end of transmission and stops when the mask receive timer expires; the Squelch command works while rx_on is low.

AGC runs while rx_on is high and keeps the slicer out of saturation: its comparator window is 3.5 times the slicer window and gain is cut until that comparator stops toggling. The gain at the falling edge of rx_on is kept in the Gain reduction state register. agc_en enables it, agc_m picks the whole reception or only the first eight subcarrier pulses, agc_alg starts from code 4h (fastest, suited to short SOF such as ISO14443A fc/128) or from 0h. Default: on, whole reception, preset algorithm.

A peak-hold RSSI runs on both channels from the rising edge of rx_on and freezes while it is low; it restarts from zero when AGC lowers the gain. The 4-bit result, 2.8 dB per step with a maximum of Dh (13), is in the RSSI display register; Clear RSSI restarts it.

Analog preset after selecting NFCIP-1 sets the receiver. Two bits in Receiver configuration register 3 serve this mode: lim clips the signal after the first and second gain stages for a close peer, and rg_nfc fixes second and third stage gain reduction at -6 dB with the slicer window at maximum.

CSO is an excitation electrode at a fixed frequency of a few hundred kHz; CSI senses the charge it induces, rectified synchronously into a DC voltage proportional to the capacitance between them and converted by the A/D in absolute mode. The electrodes tolerate up to 25 pF to ground and up to 1 MΩ leakage. A hand or a tag antenna near the electrodes raises that capacitance. Measure capacitance runs one measurement; wake-up mode can run them periodically against a stored reference or a running average.

Gain 2.8 V/pF typical by default, 6.5 V/pF maximum; with an A/D LSB of about 7.8 mV that is 2.8 fF/LSB (1.2 fF/LSB at maximum gain). A measurement takes 200 µs at 1.1 mA typical; one every 100 ms in wake-up mode averages 5.8 µA (3.6 µA of it standby).

A 5-bit calibration cancels parasitic capacitance between CSI and CSO in 0.1 pF steps over 3.1 pF, set by hand in the Capacitive sensor control register or by the Calibrate capacitive sensor command; the result is in the Capacitive sensor display register. Measure and calibrate in power-down mode only, to keep the crystal oscillator and the reader field from disturbing the result.

Setting wu with all other Operation control bits 0 enters wake-up mode. A 32 kHz RC oscillator and the wake-up timer schedule capacitive, phase and/or amplitude measurements and an IRQ goes to the host when one differs from its reference by more than its threshold. Phase and amplitude need the field on only about 20 µs, against about 5 ms of field before a polling command, and can run at reduced power (RFO normal level definition register). Register 31h selects the period (10 ms to 800 ms, default 100 ms) and the measurements; 32h to 3Dh hold four registers per measurement: configuration, reference, auto-averaged reference and last result. Configure all of them before entering wake-up mode; changes while it runs give unpredictable behaviour.

With auto-averaging the reference is recomputed after each measurement: NewAverage = OldAverage + (MeasuredValue - OldAverage) / Weight, computed on 13 bits. It starts on the first entry into wake-up mode after power-up or Set default, from the measurement display register once that is non-zero. A bit in each configuration register sets whether a measurement that raised an interrupt joins the average.

Enabled by en; an interrupt and the osc_ok bit (Auxiliary display register) report a stable frequency. An inverter with a controlled current source regulates the XTI amplitude to 1 Vpp; the start-up interrupt comes when the amplitude passes 750 mVpp. A 27.12 MHz crystal divided by two gives a 50 % duty 13.56 MHz carrier and better transmitter performance, so it is recommended; with a 13.56 MHz crystal the slicing stage bias is raised to limit pulse-width distortion. VHBR reception (fc/8 and above) requires the 27.12 MHz crystal. The oscillator also drives the MCU_CLK output.

Each timer has configuration registers set while it is stopped; changing them while it runs gives unpredictable behaviour. The Clear command stops every timer except the wake-up timer (and the no-response timer when nrt_emv = 1). The mask receive timer and no-response timer start at the end of transmission (end of EOF).

Holds rx_on low after transmission while no reply is expected; squelch runs meanwhile if enabled; no IRQ. In NFCIP-1 active mode it starts when the peer turns its field on. In low-power initial NFC target mode the host, after field detection, turns on oscillator, regulators and receiver and sends Start mask receive timer; the clock is divided by eight further (one count 512/fc), reaching about 9.6 ms.

Watches for a tag reply within a set time after transmission and flags I_nre. Set in No-response timer registers 1 and 2; nrt_step chooses 64/fc steps (4.72 µs, up to 309 ms) or 4096/fc (up to 19.8 s). With nrt_emv = 0 an IRQ comes only if it expires before a reply starts, and rx_on is forced low; a reply stops it. With nrt_emv = 1 it always raises an IRQ on expiry, ignores Clear, and forces rx_on low only if no reply is in progress. Start no-response timer restarts it to stretch the timeout (not in NFCIP-1 active mode). With a non-zero timeout, M_txe must stay clear and I_txe be read over SPI to synchronise transmitter and timer.

Its trigger comes from gptc2..gptc0 (register 11h): from start of reception (after SOF) to time a reception, or end of reception (after EOF) for the PCD to PICC response time; in NFCIP-1 active mode it times out the field turning off. IRQ on expiry. Start general purpose timer restarts it.

Used by wake-up mode, and also through Start wake-up timer in any mode except wake-up: the RC oscillator starts and an I_wt IRQ comes at the timeout set in the Wake-up timer control register. It is the timer that works when the crystal oscillator is off. Its tolerance is that of the RC oscillator.

8-bit successive approximation; the last result is in the A/D converter output register. Absolute mode: 0 V to 2 V, LSB 7.8125 mV (00h at 0 V or below, FFh at 2 V - 1 LSB or above). Relative mode: 1/6 to 5/6 of VSP_A, used only for phase measurement since the phase detector output scales with supply.

RFO and RFI signals are sliced and compared, then strongly low-pass filtered. The output falls as phase difference rises: VSP_A in phase, VSP_A/2 at 90°, 0 V in opposition. Measure phase feeds it to the A/D in relative mode, so the usable range is 30° to 150°.
Self-mixing of RFI1 and RFI2 gives a DC voltage proportional to their amplitude, which Measure amplitude feeds to the A/D.

Detects another device's RF field on RFI1. Automatically on in NFCIP-1 active modes; usable in others. Two thresholds set in the External field detector threshold register; its output is readable in the Auxiliary display register. Peer detection, 75 mVpp to 800 mVpp, runs in low-power mode and interrupts both when a field appears and when it goes away; it turns on automatically when the Bit rate definition register selects NFCIP-1 (initiator or target), or with en_fd. Collision avoidance, 25 mVpp to 800 mVpp: for normal reader operation check efd_o before turning on the field rather than using the NFC field on commands; for NFCIP-1 collision avoidance send the NFC field on command, with rfe = 0x7 recommended.

VDD (2.4 V to 5.5 V) feeds three regulators: VSP_A (analog), VSP_D (logic) and VSP_RF (transmitter). VDD_IO (1.65 V to 5.5 V) sets the level of /SS, MISO, MOSI, SCLK, IRQ and MCU_CLK through level shifters, independent of the internal supply. VSP_A and VSP_D are mandatory at 5 V, since the blocks behind them use 3.3 V devices; at 3 V they, and VSP_RF at any supply, are recommended for PSRR. Each regulator has its own ground pin, tied to VSS outside, so internal supply drops do not couple noise. Every regulator pin and AGD takes a blocking capacitor.

3.3 V supply mode (to 3.6 V) or 5 V supply mode (to 5.5 V), set by sup3V in IO configuration register 2; the default is 5 V mode, so a 3.3 V system sets the bit after power-up. In 3.3 V mode all regulators share one voltage from 2.4 V to 3.4 V; in 5 V mode VSP_RF is set from 3.9 V to 5.1 V and VSP_A, VSP_D are fixed at 3.4 V. The regulators run while en is high; with en low the part is in power-down with minimal supply current.

Improves transmitter PSRR, since transmitter supply noise is radiated and picked up by the receiver. reg_s = 0 (default): the voltage comes from Adjust regulators; reg_s = 1: from rege_3 to rege_1, in 120 mV steps from 3.9 V to 5.1 V (5 V mode) or 100 mV steps from 2.4 V to 3.4 V (3.3 V mode); default is the maximum. The Regulator and timer display register shows the actual voltage. A current limit holds it to about 200 mArms (500 mA into a short); for more transmitter current VSP_RF is tied to VDD outside (never to a voltage above VDD). Transmitter current through driver and regulator is the main dissipation, so Adjust regulators is recommended. VSP_RF is off in power-down and tied to VDD through 1 kΩ for a smooth power-up and wake.

In 3.3 V mode they follow the VSP_RF setting; in 5 V mode they are fixed at 3.4 V. They are required in 5 V mode (3.6 V devices behind them) and strongly recommended in 3.3 V mode. For low cost VSP_D can be disabled (vspd_off) and VSP_D shorted to VSP_A, or in 3.3 V mode fed from VDD if VSP_A is no more than 300 mV below VDD.

In power-down the regulators are off and a low-power block holds VSP_A and VSP_D below 3.6 V: typically 3.1 V (5 V supply) or 2.2 V (3 V supply), drawing 600 nA at 5 V. In 3.3 V supply mode it is off and its output is tied to VDD through 1 kΩ. Measure power supply reads VDD or any of the three regulator outputs.

The part is an SPI slave; the host starts every exchange, IRQ signals events and MCU_CLK can clock the host while the oscillator runs. /SS high holds the SPI in reset; keep it high when idle. MOSI is sampled on the falling SCLK edge and MISO changes on the rising edge. Transfers are bytes, MSB first; the first two bits after /SS falls choose the mode (register write, register read, FIFO load or read, direct command). Register read and write auto-increment the address. MISO is tristate except while sending, so MOSI and MISO can be joined into one bidirectional line; a 10 kΩ pull-down on MISO while tristate is enabled with miso_pd1 and miso_pd2. Registers work in any mode; the FIFO needs en set and a stable oscillator.

Write: mode bits 00, 6-bit address, then data bytes MSB first; each byte is written on the falling edge of its last clock. Raising /SS before a byte is complete drops that byte; a missing or read-only address is not written. Read: mode bits 01 and the address, then data on MISO; a missing address reads all zeros.
Mode bits 10 with C5 to C0 all 0 load 1 to 96 bytes into the FIFO; all 1 read from it. A byte cut short by /SS rising is not loaded; in a read it counts as unread and comes first next time.

Mode bits 11 and a 6-bit command code in one byte; the command runs on the falling edge of the last clock. Commands that start a process (calibration, measurement) send an IRQ when done, and no other SPI activity is allowed meanwhile. A command with immediate execution can be followed by a read, write or FIFO transfer without raising /SS.

Three interrupt registers: the Main interrupt register (six sources plus two bits pointing to the Timer and NFC and the Error and wake-up registers). An event sets its bit and drives IRQ high. The host reads registers 0x17, 0x18 and 0x19 in one go; reading clears them, except the pointer bits, which clear when their register is read. IRQ falls once every bit that raised it has been read. A masked source sets its bit but raises no IRQ.

The 96-byte FIFO does not limit frame length. In transmit, an IRQ comes when the FIFO content falls from water level + 1 to water level while the frame is not yet fully loaded (or below 4 bytes if fewer than the water level were loaded); in receive, when it rises from water level - 1 to water level. No FIFO IRQ is raised while the SPI is in FIFO load or read, so /SS must go high after each burst, and the host must serve the FIFO faster than the RF bit rate: an SCLK at least twice the bit rate is recommended. Two water levels each for receive and transmit are set in IO configuration register 1.

FIFO and both FIFO status registers clear at the start of reception. FIFO status register 1 counts unread bytes (readable during transfers, though it may change while being read). FIFO status register 2 flags an incomplete last byte (fifo_ncp, fifo_lb<2:0>, np_lb), cleared on reading, plus overflow (more than 96 bytes written, data corrupt) and underflow (read from an empty FIFO, or transmit data not supplied in time).

MCU_CLK gives the host 13.56 MHz, 6.78 MHz or 3.39 MHz from the crystal (out_cl1, out_cl0), or 32 kHz from the RC oscillator while the crystal is off (lf_clk_off). Default: 3.39 MHz with the 32 kHz clock enabled. Transparent mode requires it, since host framing must be synchronous to the carrier; it is recommended otherwise too, since noise from a host clocked by it is synchronous with the carrier and filtered by the receiver, and it helps EMC.

Returns every register to its power-up state except IO configuration registers 1 and 2 and the Operation control register, which reset only at power-up; calibration and adjust results are lost. Accepted in every mode; with en clear the FIFO and its status registers are not cleared. No chaining, no IRQ.

Stops transmission or reception, clears the FIFO, its status registers, the collision and interrupt registers, and stops every timer except the wake-up timer (and the no-response timer if nrt_emv = 1). With nfc_ar = 1 the response collision avoidance timer keeps running and the avoidance still happens; clear nfc_ar first to stop it. Sent first when preparing a transmission, before loading the FIFO (not needed for Transmit REQA or WUPA). Needs en and a stable oscillator; chaining allowed; no IRQ.

Transmit with CRC, without CRC, REQA and WUPA need tx_en. For the first two: Clear, then the number of bytes, then the FIFO data, then the command. REQA and WUPA need no Clear but the valid-bits count of the last byte (nbtx<2:0>) must be 0. Chaining allowed; no IRQ.

For NFCIP-1 active mode: the RFI inputs are watched with the collision avoidance threshold for another 13.56 MHz field. If none, tx_en is set and an I_cat IRQ follows after the NFCIP-1 minimum guard time, after which a transmit command can be sent; if a field is present an I_cac IRQ comes and the command must be repeated until it clears. Initial field ON does initial collision avoidance and Response field ON response collision avoidance, both with n from nfc_n1, nfc_n0 (Auxiliary definition register); the third command uses n = 0. The active delay time sits at the low limit of NFCIP-1, since field-off detection, host delay and the command add to it. Needs en and a stable oscillator frequency and amplitude.
Switches an NFC target from rate detection to normal mode, loads the rate found (register 1Fh) as the working bit rate and sets tr_am to match.
Presets receiver and transmitter bits from the Mode definition and Bit rate definition registers; not for subcarrier or BPSK stream modes.

Mask receive data forces rx_on low and stops framing of the receiver output, useful while a tag is processing and only noise would arrive; the effective mask is the OR of this and the mask receive timer. Unmask receive data sets rx_on high and enables framing, resetting a running mask receive timer. Both need rx_en; chaining allowed; no IRQ.

Turns on the transmitter and amplitude detector and converts its output in absolute mode. Conversion gain 0.6 VINPP/VOUT: one LSB is 13.02 mVpp on the RFI inputs, and 3 Vpp (the maximum on each RFI input) gives 1.8 V and code 1110 0110b. 25 µs max; needs en and a stable oscillator; no chaining; IRQ when done.
Runs the squelch procedure against tag or ambient noise. 500 µs max. Accepted with transmitter and receiver on, and acts only while rx_on is low. No chaining, no IRQ.

Reinitialises AGC, squelch and RSSI: stops a running squelch, clears its setting and copies in the gain reduction held in Receiver configuration register 4. Needs en and a stable oscillator; chaining allowed; no IRQ.

Turns on receiver and transmitter for maximum load and sets the regulators to maximum (5.1 V or 3.4 V). Every 300 µs VSP_RF is compared with VDD; if it is not at least 250 mV lower, the setting drops one step (120 mV or 100 mV), until the margin is met or the minimum (3.9 V or 2.4 V) is reached. 5 ms max. Needs en and a stable oscillator; refused when reg_s = 1; no chaining; IRQ when done.

Turns on transmission, measures the modulation depth and adjusts it to the target in the AM modulation depth control register; the result appears in the display register. 275 µs max; needs en and a stable oscillator; no chaining; IRQ when done.
Adjusts the capacitors switched by the TRIMx_y pins until the antenna LC tank is resonant. 250 µs max; needs en and a stable oscillator.

Turns on transmitter and phase detector and converts the output with the A/D in relative mode. Range 30° to 150°: below 30° reads FFh, above 150° reads 00h. One LSB is 0.13 % of the carrier period (0.468°); 90° falls mid-range (1000 0000b or 0111 1111b), higher codes mean less than 90°. 135° gives 31d (1Fh). 25 µs max; needs en and a stable oscillator; no chaining; IRQ when done.

RSSI clears itself and starts when rx_on rises, then holds its peak; Clear RSSI clears it and restarts the measurement while rx_on stays high, to follow changes in long messages. Needs en and a stable oscillator; chaining allowed; no IRQ.
Transparent mode starts at the rising edge of /SS after the command and lasts while /SS stays high. Needs en and a stable oscillator.

operation.topic: Calibrate capacitive sensor and measure capacitance
operation.text: Calibrate capacitive sensor (3 ms max) runs only in automatic calibration mode (all cs_mcal bits 0). Measure capacitance takes 250 µs max. Both are best run in power-down mode only, away from oscillator and field interference; no chaining; IRQ when done.

Measures VDD, VSP_A, VSP_D or VSP_RF as selected by mpsv1, mpsv0 (Regulator voltage control register) through a 1/3 divider into the A/D in absolute mode; one LSB is 23.438 mV. 25 µs max; needs en and a stable oscillator; no chaining; IRQ when done.

No dedicated test pins: CSI and CSO serve as test pins. After the Test access command, test registers outside the normal map are read and written with ordinary register commands in a chained sequence with auto-increment. They keep their content across SPI resets and return to default at power-up or with the Clear test registers command. Analog test register 01h routes internal receiver signals to CSI and CSO for observation.

The part powers up in power-down mode with registers at default. Then: set both IO configuration registers (supply mode, crystal, MCU_CLK, antenna mode); set up the regulators, preferably with Adjust regulators; for tank tuning send Calibrate antenna; for AM modulation (such as ISO14443B) write the target depth to the AM modulation depth control register, then issue Calibrate modulation depth. The part is then ready.

Write the Mode definition and Bit rate definition registers and send Analog preset, adding any other options by register. Set en to enter ready mode and wait for the oscillator interrupt. Set rx_en and tx_en; protocols want the field on for a time before the first command (5 ms for ISO14443), which the general purpose timer can measure. REQA and WUPA have their own commands; otherwise: Clear, write the number of bytes (Number of transmitted bytes registers 1 and 2), load the FIFO, send Transmit with or without CRC, and wait for the end-of-transmission IRQ. The receiver then watches RFI automatically with RSSI and AGC, framing fills the FIFO and an end-of-receive IRQ comes with the byte count in the FIFO status registers; errors and bit collisions raise their own flags. Frames longer than the FIFO are served through the water level IRQs.

Initiator mode ISO14443A (the default) in the Mode definition register and 106 kbit/s both ways in the Bit rate definition register. Set antcl (ISO14443A and NFC 106kb/s settings register) before REQA or WUPA so a collision in ATQA or anticollision raises no framing error; antcl is 1 only for REQA, WUPA and anticollision frames and 0 for every other command, and also gives correct anticollision timing and parity extraction. Set the mask receive timer below the frame delay time (FDT) and the no-response timer above it: MRT < FDT - 64/fc, NRT > FDT + 64/fc; the timers have half-step (64/fc) resolution against the 128/fc of ISO14443A so the receiver can be unmasked half a step before the reply. FDT is 1236/fc after a last bit 1, 1172/fc after a last bit 0. Send Analog preset, set rx_en and tx_en, wait the 5 ms field time. Set no_CRC_rx = 1 for REQA, WUPA and anticollision replies before SAK.

REQA and WUPA are direct commands; an IRQ marks their end and reception starts after the mask receive timer. All tags reply together with ATQA, which can collide, so any IRQ other than I_nre counts as a tag present. For several tags: REQA; anticollision and select one; HLTA it; repeat until every tag is halted and every UID read.

ANTICOLLISION and SELECT carry SEL (1 byte), NVB (1 byte) and 0 to 40 UID bits. Anticollision frames have no CRC: send with Transmit without CRC and receive with no_CRC_rx = 1. The final SELECT and its SAK carry CRC: clear no_CRC_rx and send with Transmit with CRC. A collision can fall on a byte boundary or inside a byte; in the split-byte case the invalid MSBs of the received byte are ignored, and on transmit the partial byte is padded with 0s in the MSBs, ignored according to register 1Eh. Cascade level n uses SEL 93h (4-byte UID), 95h (7-byte) or 97h (10-byte); the first frame is SEL + NVB 20h with Number of transmitted bytes registers set to 00h and 10h; expected IRQs I_txe, I_col on collision, I_rxs, I_rxe. On a collision the Collision display register gives the bit position and the next frame resends the valid bits plus the chosen bit. SELECT is SEL + NVB 70h + UID CLn; SAK says whether the UID is complete or the next cascade level follows.

212 and 424 kbit/s, the same in both directions; reader-to-tag modulation is AM. Only the payload goes in the FIFO, with its length in the Number of transmitted bytes registers; Transmit with CRC sends preamble (48 bits by default, set by f_p1, f_p0), sync, length (number of transmitted bytes + 1), payload and two CRC bytes. On reception, after preamble and sync, length and payload go to the FIFO and CRC is checked internally.

All NFCIP-1 initiator modes and active target modes at 106, 212 and 424 kbit/s. Stable active P2P needs a junction temperature below 75 °C for reliable peer detection (trg threshold) and the rfe threshold at 800 mV.

Works like reader to tag, with the initial RF collision avoidance first: check efd_o for an external field; if one is present the field cannot be turned on. After the guard time the exchange is ISO14443A (106 kbit/s) or FeliCa (212, 424 kbit/s).

At 212 and 424 kbit/s the transport frame (preamble, SB, LEN, data, CRC) matches the FeliCa and initialisation frame. At 106 kbit/s SB (F0h) and LEN appear only in the transport frame, enabled by nfc_f0 with ISO14443A at 106 kbit/s. Transmit: only transport data in the FIFO; Transmit with CRC adds F0h, length (bytes + 1) and the two CRC bytes. Receive: F0h is checked, length and data go to the FIFO, CRC is checked internally; a wrong start byte still stores the data and raises a soft framing error IRQ.

targ = 0 and NFCIP-1 active mode, then Analog preset (AM channel only, PM off, nfc_f0 set). tx_en is left clear: NFC field ON commands turn the field on and it turns off automatically after each message, held on for a time set by the general purpose timer. Entering NFCIP-1 enables the external field detector (en_fd); peer detection watches for the target field and the collision avoidance threshold is used during the field ON commands. With nfc_ar = 1 and nfc_n1, nfc_n0 = 0: NFC initial field ON gives I_cat after TIRFG; send the message; the field turns off; the no-response timer runs while waiting for the target field (IRQ on timeout); target field on gives I_eon and starts the mask receive timer, then reception as for a reader; target field off gives I_eof and starts response collision avoidance automatically, with I_cat after TARFG; loop. Clear nfc_ar before the last command (DLS_REQ) so the field stays off.

targ = 1 enables the external field detector; with targ set and the Operation control register all 0 the part sits in low-power initial NFC target mode with peer detection on. Bit rate detection mode finds the initiator rate and stores it in register 1Fh; normal mode uses the Bit rate definition register. Sequence from initial target mode with rate detection and nfc_ar = 1: I_eon; the host starts oscillator, regulators and receiver and sends Start mask receive timer; start of message gives a receive-start IRQ, rate detection gives I_nfct and stores the rate, the message goes to the FIFO; the host sends Go to normal NFC mode (chainable with the FIFO read) and sets the Tx modulation type; initiator field off gives I_eof and automatic response collision avoidance, with I_cat after TARFG; the reply is sent and the field turns off after the general purpose timer. The loop then repeats with n = 0. After the last reply (DLS_RES) the general purpose timer IRQ comes as the field turns off, the Operation control register is cleared to return to low-power target mode and the Mode definition register set back to rate detection.

tr_am selects OOK or AM; Analog preset sets AM for ISO14443B, FeliCa and NFCIP-1 212 and 424 kbit/s. The depth is set either with am_s = 0, a target in mod5 to mod0 and the Calibrate modulation depth command, or with am_s = 1 by writing register 26h (RFO AM modulated level definition) directly. Modulation index is (a - b)/(a + b), a and b the unmodulated and modulated amplitudes: ISO14443B typically 10 % (8 % to 14 %), ISO15693 10 % to 30 %, FeliCa and NFCIP-1 212/424 kbit/s 8 % to 30 %. The measured unmodulated level is divided by a binary number from 1 to 1.98 whose fractional bits are mod5 to mod0; for 10 %, a/b = 1.2222, binary 1.001110, so mod = 001110.

With oscillator and regulators on: the transmitter starts at the unmodulated level; the RFI amplitude is measured into the A/D register; the target modulated level is computed from mod5 to mod0; the driver strength is set by successive approximation to the closest level; the result goes to the AM modulation depth display register and sets the modulated level. Do not change the RFO normal level definition register afterwards, since that changes the ratio. Run Calibrate antenna first if antenna tuning is used.

With am_s = 1 the modulated level is written directly; a known setting needs no calibration. The host can also calibrate with Measure amplitude, and must for depths beyond 33 %: write the unmodulated setting (usually all 0, lowest resistance) in the RFO normal level definition register, turn on the transmitter, measure, compute the target, then step the normal level register and measure until the target is reached; finally copy that value to the RFO AM modulated level definition register and restore the normal level register.

Tuning capacitors go from the coil terminals to TRIM1_3..TRIM1_0 and TRIM2_3..TRIM2_0; with a single driver only TRIM1 is used and TRIM2 stays open. Each TRIM pin is a high-voltage NMOS switch to VSS: 50 Ω typical on for TRIM1_0, TRIM2_0 (LSB) at 3 V VSP_D, binary weighted down to 6.25 Ω for TRIM1_3, TRIM2_3. Their 25 V breakdown limits the tank peak-to-peak voltage when tuning is used. Switches of equal weight in both sets turn on and off together. Tuning runs with the Calibrate antenna command, or from the host using phase and amplitude measurements and the Antenna calibration control register.

With binary-weighted capacitors on the TRIM pins, the command searches the switch setting whose RFO-to-RFI phase is closest to the target in the Antenna calibration target register while giving the highest amplitude. A tank wired straight to the RFO pins is resonant at 90°; an EMC filter between adds its own phase shift. The target uses the Measure phase result format. The chosen setting and an error flag (target not reached) are readable afterwards; Measure phase checks the result. With trim_s = 1 the host sets the switches directly through tre_3 to tre_0.

For protocols outside the built-in framing. After the command, from the rising edge of /SS and while it stays high: MOSI drives the modulator (high = modulating), SCLK drives rx_on (high enables RSSI and AGC), MISO carries the sliced AM channel and IRQ the sliced PM channel; with one channel selected it goes to MISO and IRQ stays low. Transmitter and receiver must be on and configured first. Mode, framing and FIFO bits do nothing; other bits apply. For custom active NFC the field is turned on only during transmission by rewriting the Operation control register around each transmission, re-entering transparent mode after each SPI command; only the AM channel is needed; with en_fd set the external field detector output goes to IRQ for field detection and collision avoidance; the NFC field ON commands can be combined if their timing fits. en_fd with the Operation control register all 0 gives low-power target mode, with I_eon on an initiator field.

Bits 6 and 7 of register 05h enable custom Type A frames for MIFARE Classic compatible devices, or stream mode can be used. Stream mode keeps the ISO14443 low-level receive coding and timing inside the part and puts decoded bits in the FIFO, so the host need not work in real time. It is selected in the Mode definition register and set up in the Stream mode definition register; Analog preset does not apply. The first bit sent or received sits in the LSB of the FIFO byte.

For replies of subcarrier bursts and gaps (as ISO14443A 106 kbit/s). Subcarrier fc/64 (212 kHz) to fc/8 (1695 kHz), 2 to 8 subcarrier periods per reporting period. Each FIFO bit is 1 if subcarrier was seen in that period, 0 if not; receive starts at the first period with subcarrier and ends after more than eight periods without. Example: scf = 01b, scp = 10b gives fc/32 (424 kHz) and four periods (128/fc).

For BPSK replies (as ISO14443B). Subcarrier fc/16 (848 kHz) to fc/4 (3390 kHz), 1 to 8 periods per reporting period. Logic 0 is the first phase seen, 1 the inverted phase; receive ends at the first period without subcarrier. Example: scf = 01b, scp = 01b gives fc/8 (1695 kHz) and two periods (16/fc, about 1.18 µs).

Reader-to-tag coding comes from the FIFO: stx sets the time per FIFO bit; 0 means no modulation, 1 modulation of the current type (AM or OOK). Started by Transmit with or without CRC. Example: stx = 000b gives 128/fc (about 9.44 µs) per bit.

6-bit addresses 00h to 3Fh. Configuration registers are read/write; display registers are read only. All return to default at power-up and on Set default, except IO configuration registers 1 and 2 and the Operation control register, which reset only at power-up.
